newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher led by CPI long bonds.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher led by CPI long bonds.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly higher on Sunday led by a rise in long CPI-linked bonds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.06 pct to 102.88
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.07 pct to 101.79.
Volume was a moderate 168 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in Makams.

"The bond market is in the shadow of the stock market and investors are showing very little interest in it. Overall, trading was very quiet today," said Danniella Finn, head of sales at Batucha Securities and Investments.

"Today's main gainers were long CPI-linked bonds. Yields on these bonds are already at 4.15 percent. I believe that this trend will continue at a very slow pace and over time yields will fall below 4 percent," said Ron Weisberg at IBI Investment House.

"CPI-linked bonds are following the Makams and unlinked bonds. The Makams offer yields of 13.6 percent and 1997 inflation is expected to be 9-10 percent, which means that unlinked bonds should also offer yields of around four percent," said another trader.
Traders said Makams and unlinked bonds rose mildly in quiet trading.
Dollar-linked bonds also rose mildly following the decline of the shekel against the U.S. currency on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
